The Big Question

🧑‍💻 You write: print(\"Hello\")

But the CPU only executes machine code (binary).

❌ Common misconception...

"The CPU understands Python/Java directly."

✅ Translators bridge the gap.

Compilers, interpreters, and assemblers turn code into machine code.

High-Level Languages (HLL)

High-level languages are designed to be easy for humans to read and write.

They are often portable (can run on many different computers).

Examples
  • Python
  • Java
  • C++
Code Example 
Sum = Num1 + Num2
Deep Dive: Low-Level Languages

Deep Dive: Low-Level Languages

Languages closer to the hardware. Hard for humans, fast for machines.

1. Machine Code

Binary instructions (1s and 0s) executed directly by the CPU.

1010 0101 1100

2. Assembly Language

Uses Mnemonics (short codes) to represent machine code.

LDA First
ADD Second
STO Sum

Comparison

High-Level
  • Easy to debug
  • Portable
  • Slower execution
Low-Level
  • Fast execution
  • Hardware control
  • Hard to learn
Why use Assembly?

To write device drivers or code that needs to run extremely fast (e.g. games engines).

Did You Know?

Different CPUs, Different Code

Machine code depends on the CPU architecture (e.g., x86 vs ARM).

That’s why software often needs to be compiled for the right platform.

Phones Are ARM

Most smartphones use ARM processors.

Apps are built/translated to run on that hardware.

Translators

Software that converts code into machine code.

Assembler

Assembly → Machine Code.

Compiler

HLL → Machine Code (All at once).

Interpreter

HLL → Machine Code (Line by line).

Deep Dive: Compiler vs Interpreter

Deep Dive: Compiler vs Interpreter

Crucial for the exam!

Compiler

  • Translates whole program at once.
  • Creates an Executable (.exe) file.
  • Reports errors at the end.
  • Use: Distributing finished software.

Interpreter

  • Translates one line at a time.
  • Does NOT create an executable.
  • Stops at the first error.
  • Use: Developing/Testing code.

Scenario Check

You want to sell a video game you made. You don't want people to see or steal your source code. Which translator do you use?

Compiler

It creates a standalone .exe file. The user doesn't need the source code or the translator installed.

The IDE

IDE (Integrated Development Environment) provides tools to write, run, and debug code in one place.

Examples: PyCharm, Visual Studio, IDLE.

Deep Dive: Features

Deep Dive: IDE Features

Code Editor
Writes text. Uses Prettyprinting (colour coding) to make code readable.
Translator
Built-in Compiler or Interpreter to run code instantly.
Debugger
Finds logic errors. Uses Breakpoints and Variable Watch.
Error Diagnostics
Highlights syntax errors as you type.
Auto-completion
Predicts commands to speed up typing.
Auto-correction
Suggests fixes for common mistakes.

Quick Check

Which translator creates an executable file?

Compiler — it translates the whole program into an executable.

Quick Check

Which IDE feature helps you find logic errors by stepping through code?

Debugger

True or False?

Answer these misconception checks in your book:

  1. "A compiler translates code line by line while the program runs."
  2. "An assembler converts assembly language into machine code."
  3. "Prettyprinting is a debugger feature that executes code step-by-step."

Press Down to reveal answers

Question 1

"A compiler translates code line by line while the program runs."

Answer: False

A compiler translates the whole program first, producing an executable. An interpreter runs line-by-line.

Question 2

"An assembler converts assembly language into machine code."

Answer: True

Assemblers translate mnemonics directly into the binary opcodes the CPU executes.

Question 3

"Prettyprinting is a debugger feature that executes code step-by-step."

Answer: False

Prettyprinting is formatting/syntax colouring. Stepping through code is done with the debugger.

Key Takeaways

🧑‍💻 HLL is easier to write; LLL is closer to hardware.

🧩 Machine code is binary instructions executed by the CPU.

🏗️ Translators convert code → machine code.

🧾 Compiler translates whole program; interpreter runs line-by-line.

🧷 Assembler translates assembly mnemonics to machine code.

🧰 IDE adds tools like editor, debugger, and error diagnostics.
